title: Cyril of Jerusalem's lectures
hookLine: talks to the newly baptized explaining what they had just experienced

cards: Jerusalem, the days after Easter. A group of people come back to church who were baptized only days ago.
They had been taught the creed and the stories, but nobody had walked them through what would actually happen to them. They went in, and it happened: words, oil, water, bread.
Now they sit down, still a little dazed, and the bishop stands up. In effect he says: you've been through it. Now I'll tell you what it meant.
The talks known as Cyril's lectures to the newly baptized are that explanation.

teach.h: FIRST THE NIGHT, THEN THE WORDS.
teach.b: These talks have a name: mystagogy. The first thing the bishop says explains the order.
He had long wanted to speak to them about these mysteries, but seeing persuades more than hearing, so he waited until they had seen for themselves. First the night. Then the words.
Then he walks them back through it.

teach.h: TURN FROM THE WEST TO THE EAST.
teach.b: Remember, he says, how you stood in the outer hall, facing west, the direction of darkness, stretched out your hand and renounced Satan. Then you turned to the east, toward the light.
Remember how you took off your old garment, were anointed with oil, were led to the pool, and were asked whether you believed in the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
Every gesture had a meaning, and now he gives it to them. Then the altar. He quotes the psalm sung at communion.
In the Douay-Rheims it reads: "O taste, and see that the Lord is sweet." And he gives a very practical instruction. When you come forward, don't come with your fingers spread.
Make your left hand a throne for the right, because the right hand is about to receive a King. Hollow your palm, receive the Body of Christ, and answer Amen.

teach.h: FROM THE SIGN TO WHAT IT SIGNIFIES.
teach.b: The Catechism of the Catholic Church uses the word mystagogy for teaching that moves from the visible to the invisible, from the sign to the thing it signifies.
The water, the oil, the open hand.

how: In the Catholic Church the time after adult baptism at the Easter Vigil is called mystagogy: the newly baptized keep meeting during the Easter season to reflect on the sacraments they have received.

o: the secret rites a church keeps hidden from outsiders
the lessons given before someone may be baptized
teaching after baptism, from the signs to their meaning

s: Cyril explained the rites in detail before baptism

Cyril tells the newly baptized to make a throne of their hands for communion

games.q: you're the bishop. your candidates want to know exactly what will happen the night they're baptized. what do you do?
o: explain every rite in detail beforehand.
let them go through it, then explain it afterward.
games.why: he waited. seeing, he said, persuades more than hearing, so the meaning came after the night itself.

practice: Pick a sacrament you've received or watched, a baptism, communion, a wedding, an anointing, or, if you're new to all this, a ritual you've seen at a wedding or a funeral.
Walk through it one piece at a time, water, oil, a ring, bread in an open hand, and ask of each: what is this pointing to? If you're not sure, just let the question stay.

wordCard.voice: Mystagogy. Teaching given after the rite, leading the newly baptized from what they saw to what it means. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: mystagogy — the name for teaching that unfolds the sacraments after they are received.

carryVoice: Your line: after, the meaning. First the night, then the words that explain it. Until tomorrow.
